name: Jos Plateau
summary: Volcanic highland in central Nigeria with a cooler climate and tin-mining history.
description: The Jos Plateau is a granite and volcanic upland rising sharply above the surrounding plains. Tin and columbite mining shaped 20th-century Jos. The height brings lower temperatures, Irish potatoes and vegetables, and tourism. Gully erosion is a modern hazard.
character: Inselbergs, temperate crops, mining scars, tourism.
economy: Tourism, remnant mining, highland farming, Jos urban services.

name: Mambilla Plateau
summary: Nigeria's highest inhabited plateau on the Cameroon border in Taraba.
description: Mambilla is a grassland plateau with tea estates and a proposed mega hydropower project. Chappal Waddi (Gangirwal) in the Gashaka-Gumti / border highlands is often cited as Nigeria's highest peak. Access is via steep escarpment roads.
character: Tea, cattle, montane grassland, cloud forest fragments.
economy: Tea, livestock, proposed hydropower, limited tourism.

name: Mandara Mountains
summary: Volcanic range along the Nigeria–Cameroon border in southern Borno / northern Adamawa fringe.
description: The Mandara are culturally associated with hill peoples (Mandara, Sukur UNESCO cultural landscape on the Cameroon side). On the Nigerian side they form a rugged border highland above the Chad plains.
character: Terraced hills, volcanic plugs, border cultures.

name: Niger Delta
summary: Africa's largest wetland delta where the Niger meets the Atlantic; Nigeria's petroleum heartland.
description: The delta covers ~70,000 km² of mangrove, freshwater swamp, and barrier islands. It holds the bulk of Nigeria's oil and gas, a dense creek network, and highly politicised environmental and federal-revenue issues.
elevationNote: Mostly near sea level; tidal mangrove
character: Mangrove, oilfields, riverine settlements, barrier islands.
economy: Oil and gas, fisheries, boat transport, refining.

name: Sokoto Basin
summary: Semi-arid sedimentary basin of the northwest drained by the Sokoto–Rima system.
description: Cretaceous–Tertiary sediments underlie millet, sorghum, and irrigated fadama. The basin is drought-prone and depends on dams and groundwater. It is the core landscape of the Caliphate northwest.
character: Sahel–Sudan plains, seasonal rivers, irrigation schemes.
economy: Grain, livestock, onions (dry-season irrigation), limited oil exploration historically.

name: Guinea Savanna
summary: Wooded savanna belt between southern rainforest and northern Sudan/Sahel savanna.
description: Guinea savanna (southern and northern Guinea) is Nigeria's broad middle belt: shea, yam, sorghum, and cattle routes. Rainfall is typically 900–1,500 mm. It includes much of Kwara, Niger, Kogi, Benue, Nasarawa, and parts of Kaduna and FCT.
character: Parkland trees, seasonal burn, mixed farming.
economy: Yam, shea, grains, livestock corridors, Abuja hinterland.

name: Idanre Hills
summary: Dramatic granite inselberg cluster and UNESCO-adjacent cultural landscape in Ondo State.
description: Idanre Hills rise abruptly above the Ondo plain with steep ascents, ancient Oke-Idanre settlement ruins, and panoramic views. The hills are a major tourism and pilgrimage destination in southwestern Nigeria.
character: Granite domes, sacred groves, heritage settlement.

name: Shere Hills
summary: Rocky highland within the Jos Plateau and a popular hiking destination.
description: Shere Hills form a jagged granite skyline near Jos with peaks including Peak 1 (~1,829 m). Rock climbing, hiking, and cool-climate tourism draw visitors from across Nigeria.
character: Granite tors, hiking trails, cool climate.

name: Udi–Nsukka Escarpment
summary: Eastern Nigeria escarpment above the Cross River basin; Enugu coal belt.
description: The Udi Hills and Nsukka escarpment mark the edge of the Enugu Plateau. Coal seams here fuelled Nigeria's railway era. The ridge now hosts Enugu city, universities, and forest patches.
character: Coal measures, forest patches, university towns.
economy: Coal heritage, Enugu urban economy, education.

name: Oban Hills
summary: Cross River rainforest highlands linked to the Oban sector of Cross River National Park.
description: Oban Hills lie in the Cross River–Cameroon biodiversity hotspot with lowland and montane rainforest, drill monkeys, and forest elephants (rare). Terrain is rugged and heavily forested.

name: Aso Rock
summary: Iconic granite inselberg dominating Abuja's skyline and the Presidential Villa.
description: Aso Rock is a 400-metre monolith at the heart of the Federal Capital Territory. It gives its name to Aso Villa (Presidential residence) and is visible across Abuja's Central Area.
elevationNote: ~936 m summit; ~400 m relief above plain
character: Granite monolith, seat of government backdrop.

name: Zuma Rock
summary: Massive monolith on the Abuja–Kaduna corridor, nicknamed the Gateway to Abuja.
description: Zuma Rock rises ~725 m above the surrounding plain near Madalla in Niger State. Its distinctive face is visible from the Abuja–Kaduna expressway and features in Nigerian iconography.
elevationNote: ~725 m above surrounding plain (~1,125 m AMSL)

name: Olumo Rock
summary: Historic Egba refuge rock in Abeokuta, Ogun State.
description: Olumo Rock served as a natural fortress during 19th-century inter-tribal wars. Today it is a major cultural tourism site with caves, carvings, and views over Abeokuta.

name: Chappal Waddi (Gangirwal)
summary: Nigeria's highest point (~2,419 m) on the Mambilla / Gashaka border highlands.
description: Chappal Waddi (also Gangirwal) lies in the Gashaka-Gumti / Mambilla border highlands in Taraba State. The peak is often cited as Nigeria's highest ground, in montane grassland and forest ecotone.
character: Montane grassland, border highlands, cloud forest fringe.

name: Wadi Kuru Peak
summary: Notable peak on the Jos Plateau used for mountaineering practice.
description: Wadi Kuru is among the recognised high points on the Jos Plateau near Jos city, popular with hikers and mountaineering clubs.
